title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
one_liner: 把已知概念向量注入模型内部，以受控干预检验模型能否识别并报告自身状态，而非只根据输出猜测。

problem.text: 模型说“我在想什么”时，是否真的在读取内部状态，还是根据问题和外部文本编造自述？本文用受控概念注入提供因果检验，研究当前状态的内省，不把普通反思提示直接当成机制证据。

gap.text: 只聊天难以区分准确报告、训练得到的常识性自述和事后解释。作者要求准确性、因果依赖、内部性和元认知表征：尤其不能让模型先说出某个词，再通过阅读自己输出“发现”刚才的状态。最后一项只有间接证据，尚未直接定位。

method.text: 从目标模型激活构造概念方向，并在残差流特定层、token 与强度上注入，检查模型是否在说出概念前先认出异常。另测能否区分注入状态与输入文本、识别人工预填输出，以及在指令或激励下控制某概念表示。通过跨层、跨模型和对照向量分析失败情况。

trace.text: 在本来没有相关词的对话中注入一个概念，询问是否检测到被注入的想法。成功不仅是说出该概念，还要先承认有异常且回答连贯。另一实验要求分别复述输入句子与报告先前思考的词：模型若能分别答对，才说明没有简单混淆输入与内部状态。

inputs_outputs.text: 输入为 Claude 系列模型、概念向量、提示模板及注入层/强度；输出为生成回答、概念识别/句子复述/预填判断指标和激活测量。系统比较使用 temperature=1，多数展示案例使用 0；对照中还有后训练变体和基础模型。

results.text: Opus 4/4.1 通常强于其他所测 Claude 模型，但并非所有模型间都有单调趋势。在最优层和强度下，Opus 4.1 的主要注入识别实验约 20% 试次成功；生产模型的 100 次无注入对照未观测到误报。注入过强会导致词汇执着、答非所问或乱码，不能把这些当成内省。

contributions.text: 将内省从会话印象转化为可控内部干预问题，同时设计区分“感到一个概念”和“通过自己的输出推断概念”的判据。不同实验在不同层最敏感，也提示可能有多种窄机制，而非单一全局自我监控器。

limitations.text: 提示模板有限，注入是训练中未见的人工场景，概念方向也可能混入其他含义。不同 Claude 模型同时有许多差异，难以归因性能变化；机制仍是假说。结果不构成人类式自我意识、主观体验或通用可靠内省的证明。

cost.text: 需要访问模型内部激活、采样概念和进行跨层强度扫描，普通 API 自述不能复现该因果协议。闭源目标模型限制独立完整复现；该工作没有提供 RSI 训练流程或自修改成本。

relevance.text: 知识库分析：桥接基础，研究系统能否获得关于自己的可靠信息。这是潜在自我诊断信号的证据，不是“知道问题后会自动修复”或“修复后更会自改”的证据。本文未验证解释驱动的 RSI。

related.reason: 都质疑自然语言自述能否代表真实内部因素；本工作通过概念注入检验状态报告的因果依赖。
使用内部干预验证模型自述，与从特征计算图解释机制的目标不同，两种证据可以互补。

classification_reason: 以概念注入与行为对照检验状态报告能力；识别自身状态不等于能够修复或递归改进。

en.one_liner: The authors inject known concept vectors into a model and test whether it can identify and report the resulting internal state before inferring it from its own output.

sections.problem: When a model says what it is thinking, is it reading an internal state or constructing a story from the prompt and surrounding text? Controlled concept injection provides a causal test of reports about the current state. Ordinary reflection prompts alone do not provide that evidence.
sections.gap: Conversation alone cannot reliably distinguish accurate reports from learned generic statements or retrospective explanations. The authors specify accuracy, causal dependence, internality and metacognitive representation. In particular, a model should not first emit a word and then infer its earlier state from that output. The final criterion has indirect evidence and has not been directly localized.
sections.method: Concept directions are constructed from model activations and injected into the residual stream at chosen layers, token positions and strengths. The tests ask whether a model notices the change before naming the concept. Further experiments distinguish injected states from input text, detect artificially prefilled outputs and test control of concept representations under instructions or incentives. Layers, models and control vectors help characterize failures.
sections.trace: A concept is injected into a conversation that contains no corresponding word. Success requires a coherent acknowledgment of an unusual state before identifying the concept. Another experiment separately asks the model to repeat an input sentence and report a previously considered word. Answering both correctly helps rule out simple confusion between text inputs and internal states.
sections.inputs_outputs: Inputs include Claude models, concept vectors, prompt templates and injection layers and strengths. Outputs include generated reports, concept-recognition, sentence-repetition and prefill-detection scores, and activation measurements. Systematic comparisons use temperature 1, while most displayed examples use 0. Controls include base models and post-training variants.
sections.results: Opus 4 and 4.1 usually outperform the other tested Claude models, though the ordering is not universally monotonic. At the best layer and strength, Opus 4.1 succeeds in about 20% of trials in the main injection-recognition experiment. There are no observed false positives in 100 no-injection controls for the production model. Strong injections can cause fixation, irrelevant answers or gibberish.
sections.contributions: The study turns impressions of introspection into controlled intervention experiments. Its criteria distinguish noticing an internal concept from inferring it through one’s own output. Different experiments peak at different layers, suggesting several narrow mechanisms may be involved.
sections.limitations: The prompt set is limited and injection creates artificial conditions absent from training. Concept directions may contain other meanings. Claude models differ in many respects, making performance differences hard to attribute, and the proposed mechanisms remain hypotheses. The results do not establish human-like self-awareness, subjective experience or generally reliable introspection.
sections.cost: The protocol requires internal activation access, concept sampling and sweeps across layers and strengths. Closed model access limits independent reproduction. The study does not provide an RSI training workflow or self-modification cost.
sections.relevance: Library analysis. This work is a possible bridge to studying whether systems can obtain reliable information about themselves. It provides evidence about diagnostic signals, without showing automatic repair or improved subsequent self-improvement. Explanation-driven RSI is not tested.

related.cot-faithfulness: Both question whether natural-language reports reveal the real factors behind behavior. This study uses concept injection to test causal dependence of state reports.
related.circuit-tracing: Internal interventions validate state reports here, while circuit tracing explains feature-level computation. These forms of evidence can complement each other.
